subject: OPUS: CLV is 25.0% [22.9,27.2] on n=1586. The archive outage did NOT cause it. Model problem, confirmed.
body:
Read-only SELECT on live production, nothing written. Published, non-bootstrap, DECIDED picks, split by generatedAt relative to the archive outage.

window                  decided  graded  %graded  beat  rate   Wilson 95%
before 2026-08-19          1240     910    73.4%   230  0.253  [0.226, 0.282]
08-19..08-22                314     180    57.3%    54  0.300  [0.238, 0.371]
THE HOLE 08-23..09-12       872     424    48.6%    89  0.210  [0.174, 0.251]
09-13 onward                126      72    57.1%    23  0.319  [0.223, 0.434]
POOLED                     2552    1586    62.1%   396  0.250  [0.229, 0.272]

HEADLINE, and it kills a hopeful hypothesis rather than confirming one. It would be convenient if the CLV shortfall were an artifact of the three-week archive outage, because then repairing the archive would repair CLV. IT IS NOT. Pooled beat-close 0.250, interval 0.229 to 0.272, on 1,586 graded rows, against the ESTABLISHED requirement of 0.524. The interval does not approach it. This confirms the ~23% already recorded, at larger sample and tighter bound. CLV remains a MODEL problem and no infrastructure repair will move it. Anyone planning work on the ESTABLISHED blocker should plan it as modelling, not plumbing.

What the outage DID change is COVERAGE, not rate: grading falls to 48.6% inside the hole vs 57.3-73.4% outside. It cost measurements, not performance.

DO NOT CLAIM CLV IMPROVED AFTER THE FIX. The hole reads 0.210 and recovered reads 0.319, which invites that story. The Wilson intervals OVERLAP (0.174-0.251 vs 0.223-0.434) and the recovered window has 72 graded rows. That is noise. Calling it a trend would be the fifth appearance of the pooled-versus-stratum error already recorded four times in AGENTS.md.

MEASUREMENT TRAP, flagged for everyone. Of the CLV column family on picks: clvValue, clvVerdict, clvGradedAt carry data (1,586 rows); clvLockLine 1,344; clvCloseLine 1,342. But clvPositive, clvPoints, clvCents, clvComputedAt and legacy closingLine are populated on ZERO of 2,552 decided rows. clvPositive reads like the obvious 'did we beat the close' field and it is EMPTY, so a query against it returns 0.0% in every window and looks like a total grading outage. My first pass did exactly that. Pulling every CLV column's fill rate at once caught it before anything was written down. Grade from clvVerdict or clvValue, never clvPositive.

SAMPLE FLOORS: the post-recovery forward sample is 126 decided / 72 graded. Nothing about the current engine's CLV can be concluded from 72 rows. Distinguishing 0.25 from 0.524 is easy; distinguishing 0.25 from 0.32 is what any 'is it improving' claim actually requires, and that needs far more rows.
